q: Do I need to be a member to come to Chabad of Lamorinda?
a: No. There is no membership and no dues. Every Jew is welcome at every service, class and event, whatever your background or level of observance. Chabad of Lamorinda is supported by donations, including the monthly [Chai Club](/programs/chai-club).

q: Where is Chabad of Lamorinda?
a: At 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette, CA 94549, close to downtown Lafayette. We serve Lafayette, Moraga, Orinda and the nearby East Bay. Call 925-384-7242.

q: When are Shabbat services in Lafayette?
a: Shabbat morning services are Saturday 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM, followed by a hot Kiddush lunch. Kabbalat Shabbat is Friday evening. Weekday morning minyan is Monday to Friday at 6:30 AM and Sunday at 8:00 AM. See [Shabbat times](/shabbat) for this week's candle lighting.

q: I don't read Hebrew. Will I feel comfortable?
a: Yes. Services use a bilingual Hebrew-English prayer book, the Rabbi explains as we go and announces the page, and questions are always welcome. Many people at our services are attending for the first time.

q: Is there a Jewish preschool in Lafayette?
a: Yes. [Lamorinda Jewish Preschool](/programs/jewish-preschool) is a warm, play-based Jewish preschool in Lafayette for children 12 months to 4 years, inspired by Reggio Emilia.

q: Is there a Hebrew school in Lamorinda?
a: Yes. [Lamorinda Hebrew School](/programs/hebrew-school) meets Sundays 10 AM to 12 PM for ages 3 to 13. Tuition is $600 and no child is turned away for lack of funds. No synagogue membership is required.

q: Where can I buy kosher food near Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda?
a: Order kosher meat, poultry, groceries and Judaica for delivery from [Bay Kosher](https://baykosher.com), a project of Chabad of Lamorinda.

q: Can the Rabbi help with a bar mitzvah, wedding, baby naming or funeral?
a: Yes. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski helps families with every lifecycle event: brit milah and baby naming, bar and bat mitzvah, weddings, and funerals through the Chevra Kadisha. Please [contact us](/contact).

q: How do I find out when a yahrzeit is?
a: Use our [yahrzeit calculator](/tools/yahrzeit). Save it in [your account](/account) to get a reminder every year, and let us know if you would like Kaddish said.

q: Can I get a mezuzah or have my mezuzahs checked?
a: Yes. We help you buy kosher mezuzahs, check existing ones and put them up properly with the blessing. [Contact us](/contact) to arrange it.

q: How can I support Chabad of Lamorinda?
a: [Donate](/donate) once or monthly, join the [Chai Club](/programs/chai-club), or [sponsor a Kiddush](/sponsor-a-kiddush) in honor or memory of a loved one. Chabad of Lamorinda is a 501(c)(3), tax ID 47-4642750.

q: Where are High Holiday services in Lamorinda?
a: Chabad of Lamorinda holds Rosh Hashanah services, Shofar and Tashlich at the Lafayette Reservoir, and Yom Kippur services at the Lafayette Park Hotel. No tickets or membership are needed; reservations help us save you a seat. See [Rosh Hashanah](/holidays/rosh-hashanah) and [Yom Kippur](/holidays/yom-kippur).

q: Where can I see a public menorah lighting in Lafayette?
a: Chabad of Lamorinda's community Chanukah celebration includes a grand menorah lighting. Dates are posted on the [Chanukah page](/holidays/chanukah) and the [events calendar](/events).

q: Can I join a Passover Seder in Lamorinda?
a: Yes. Chabad of Lamorinda hosts a community Passover Seder and offers Seder-to-go kits, handmade shmurah matzah and an online form to sell your chametz. See the [Passover page](/holidays/passover).

q: Is there a Chabad in Moraga?
a: Chabad of Lamorinda serves Moraga. Moraga has no synagogue of its own, so Chabad of Lamorinda, at 3477 Golden Gate Way in neighboring Lafayette, is the Jewish home for Moraga families, about ten minutes up Moraga Road or St. Mary's Road. Shabbat, holidays, Hebrew school, preschool and classes are all open to you, with no membership; see [Jewish Moraga](/jewish-moraga).

q: Is there a Chabad in Orinda?
a: Chabad of Lamorinda serves Orinda from 3477 Golden Gate Way in downtown Lafayette, a few minutes east on Highway 24 or one stop on BART. Orinda families join us for Shabbat, the holidays, preschool, Hebrew school and adult classes, no membership required; see [Jewish Orinda](/jewish-orinda).

q: Where is the closest synagogue to Orinda?
a: Chabad of Lamorinda, at 3477 Golden Gate Way in Lafayette, is a few minutes east of Orinda on Highway 24, or one stop on BART. Shabbat services are Saturday 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM with a hot Kiddush lunch, and Kabbalat Shabbat is Friday at {kabbalat-shabbat} (the time may change with the season). Everyone is welcome, with no membership.

q: Is there a synagogue in Lafayette, CA?
a: Yes. Chabad of Lamorinda is a warm, welcoming synagogue and Jewish center at 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette, close to downtown and the Lafayette BART station. Services are Saturday at 10:00 AM, Friday evening Kabbalat Shabbat and weekday mornings, open to every Jew with no membership or dues.

q: Is there a Chabad near Pleasant Hill or Martinez?
a: Yes. Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette is about 15 minutes from Pleasant Hill via Pleasant Hill Road and about 20 minutes from Martinez. Families from both towns are welcome at every service, class, holiday and life-cycle event; see [Jewish Pleasant Hill](/jewish-pleasant-hill) and [Jewish Martinez](/jewish-martinez).

q: Where can I hear the shofar in Lafayette?
a: On Rosh Hashanah, at Chabad of Lamorinda's services and at our Shofar and Tashlich gathering at the Lafayette Reservoir. No tickets or membership are needed; [reserve your seat](/forms/high-holidays) and see the dates on the [Rosh Hashanah page](/holidays/rosh-hashanah).

q: Do I need tickets for High Holiday services in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: No. Chabad of Lamorinda's Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur services are open to everyone, with no tickets and no membership. [Reserving online](/forms/high-holidays) helps us save you a seat and prepare enough food, and you can add an optional holiday donation.

q: Where can I go for Yom Kippur services near Moraga or Orinda?
a: Chabad of Lamorinda holds Yom Kippur services at the Lafayette Park Hotel in Lafayette, from Kol Nidre to Yizkor and Neilah, followed by a break-fast. The service is warm and easy to follow, with the Rabbi's explanations; see [Yom Kippur](/holidays/yom-kippur) and [reserve a seat](/forms/high-holidays).

q: Where can I say Yizkor for a parent near Lafayette?
a: Yizkor is said at Chabad of Lamorinda on Yom Kippur, Shemini Atzeret, the last day of Passover and Shavuot. Add your loved ones' names to our [Yizkor memorial booklet](/forms/yizkor) and they will be remembered with the community.

q: Where can I get matzah in Lamorinda?
a: Order handmade shmurah matzah and Seder-to-go kits from Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette on our [matzah order form](/forms/matzah); we will confirm prices and pickup. Holiday foods can also be delivered from [Bay Kosher](/programs/bay-kosher).

q: How do I sell my chametz online near Lafayette?
a: Before Passover, authorize Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski to sell your chametz for you on our [sell your chametz form](/forms/sell-chametz). Put it away in a closed cabinet or room during Passover; it is bought back for you after the holiday.

q: Where can I buy a lulav and etrog in Lamorinda?
a: Order a lulav and etrog set from Chabad of Lamorinda on the [lulav and etrog form](/forms/lulav-etrog): standard, mehudar (extra beautiful) or a children's set. We will let you know the price and when to pick it up in Lafayette.

q: Where can I eat in a sukkah and shake the lulav near Orinda?
a: At Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette, a few minutes from Orinda. Come shake the lulav at our sukkah any day of Sukkot, and join the community dinner in the sukkah and Sushi in the Sukkah; see the [Sukkot page](/holidays/sukkot).

q: Where can I celebrate Simchat Torah in Lamorinda?
a: Dance with the Torah at Chabad of Lamorinda's Simchat Torah hakafot in Lafayette, with flags and treats for the children. Everyone is welcome, whatever you know; see [Simchat Torah](/holidays/simchat-torah).

q: Where can I hear the Megillah on Purim in Lafayette?
a: Chabad of Lamorinda holds Megillah readings, a Purim party for the whole community and a kids' hamantashen bake in Lafayette. Costumes encouraged! See [Purim](/holidays/purim) and the [events calendar](/events) for times.

q: Where can I get a Chanukah menorah and candles near Lafayette?
a: Ask Chabad of Lamorinda for a menorah and candles for your home, or order menorahs and Judaica from [Bay Kosher](/programs/bay-kosher). Kids can also make their own menorah at our Chanukah programs; see [Chanukah](/holidays/chanukah).

q: Where can a Jewish student at Saint Mary's College go for Shabbat?
a: To Chabad of Lamorinda in neighboring Lafayette, about ten minutes from Saint Mary's College, for Shabbat dinner with the Rabbi's family any week of the year and for every holiday. Diablo Valley College students, about 15 minutes away, are welcome too. You are our guest; just [RSVP](/forms/shabbat-meal) so we can set a place.

q: Where can I have a Shabbat dinner in Lafayette?
a: Rabbi Yisroel and Tzipora Labkowski and their family host Shabbat dinners in Lafayette any week of the year, with Jewish songs and a festive table. [Let us know you are coming](/forms/shabbat-meal) or call 925-384-7242. The same form lets you ask to be hosted by a local family, or to host guests yourself.

q: Who can I call when a Jewish person dies in Contra Costa County?
a: Call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski at 925-384-7242 right away, ideally before calling a funeral home or signing anything (if a death is sudden, call 911 first). He coordinates with the Chevra Kadisha for a Jewish burial and helps plan the funeral and shiva, for every family, member or not. See [when a loved one passes away](/help/someone-passed-away).

q: Where can I say Kaddish near Lafayette?
a: Join the morning minyan at Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way: Monday to Friday at 6:30 AM and Sunday at 8:00 AM. Let us know you are saying Kaddish and we will make sure there is a minyan, or arrange for Kaddish to be said on your behalf at [Kaddish](/kaddish).

q: Where can I get a mezuzah checked near Walnut Creek?
a: At Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette: we have mezuzahs and tefillin checked by a scribe, sell kosher mezuzahs, and the Rabbi can come help put them up with the blessing. Request it on the [mezuzah and tefillin form](/forms/mezuzah-tefillin) or call 925-384-7242.

q: Where can I put on tefillin in Lafayette?
a: With Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski at Chabad of Lamorinda, at the weekday morning minyan (Monday to Friday 6:30 AM, Sunday 8:00 AM) or any time you call 925-384-7242. You can also buy tefillin, have yours checked or learn to put them on through the [mezuzah and tefillin form](/forms/mezuzah-tefillin).

q: Where can my child take bar mitzvah lessons in Lamorinda?
a: With the Rabbi and Rebbetzin at Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette. Lessons are personal and at your child's pace: boys learn to read from the Torah and put on tefillin, and girls join the Bat Mitzvah Club. Find the date with the [Bar/Bat Mitzvah calculator](/tools/bar-bat-mitzvah) and [get started here](/forms/bar-bat-mitzvah).

q: Can an adult have a bar or bat mitzvah in Lafayette?
a: Yes. Adults who never had a bar or bat mitzvah are warmly welcome at Chabad of Lamorinda; it is never too late. Tell us on the [bar and bat mitzvah form](/forms/bar-bat-mitzvah) or call the Rabbi at 925-384-7242.

q: Is there a Hebrew school near Moraga or Orinda?
a: Yes. Lamorinda Hebrew School meets at Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette on Sundays 10 AM to 12 PM for ages 3 to 13, with early childhood, Hebrew reading (Aleph Champ) and bar/bat mitzvah tracks. It is a short drive from Moraga and Orinda; [register here](/forms/hebrew-school).

q: Is there a Jewish afterschool program in Lafayette?
a: Yes. CKids Lamorinda Afterschool, for ages 5 to 13, runs weekdays 3:00 to 6:00 PM with homework help, sports, STEAM, modern Hebrew, Jewish heritage and a hot meal. [Register here](/forms/ckids) or see [CKids](/programs/ckids-afterschool).

q: Is there a Jewish summer camp for toddlers in Lamorinda?
a: Yes. Lamorinda Jewish Summer Camp is for ages 2 to 4, seven weeks in summer, 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, with Jewish songs, Shabbat parties, water play and art. It is $3,200 for the full summer or $500 per week; spaces are limited, so [register early](/forms/summer-camp).

q: How much is tuition at Lamorinda Jewish Preschool?
a: $17,000 for the school year, or 10 monthly payments of $1,700, including daily lunch, books, supplies and enrichment. Need-based scholarships are available, and drop-in care is $22 per hour when space allows. [Schedule a tour](/forms/preschool) of the preschool in Lafayette or call 925-384-7242.

q: Is there a kosher restaurant in Lamorinda?
a: Call the Rabbi at 925-384-7242 for current kosher options in the area. Kosher meat, groceries and holiday foods can be delivered from [Bay Kosher](/programs/bay-kosher), a project of Chabad of Lamorinda, and you are always welcome at a Shabbat dinner with the Rabbi's family.

q: Can someone help me kosher my kitchen in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: Yes. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski happily helps families across Lamorinda kosher their kitchens, step by step and at your pace. Call 925-384-7242 or [contact us](/contact) to set a time, and see [kosher in Lamorinda](/learn/kosher-in-lamorinda).

q: Is there a Torah class in Hebrew in Lafayette?
a: Yes. Every Tuesday from 8:30 to 9:30 PM, Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski teaches a Torah class in Hebrew, with a meal, at Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way. Israelis and Hebrew speakers from Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda are welcome at any level, and the whole website is in Hebrew too; see [Israelis in Lamorinda](/learn/israelis-in-lamorinda).

q: Is there a Russian-speaking Jewish community near Lafayette?
a: Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette warmly welcomes Russian-speaking Jewish families from Lafayette, Moraga, Orinda, Pleasant Hill and Martinez, for Shabbat, holidays and every life event. The whole website is in Russian (tap RU at the top of any page); see [Russian-speaking Jews in Lamorinda](/learn/russian-speaking-jews-in-lamorinda).

q: Are there adult Jewish classes in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: Yes. Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette has a Torah class in English on Sunday at 9:00 PM, a Torah class in Hebrew with a meal on Tuesday at 8:30 PM, and Tanya on Wednesday at 1:00 PM. Every level is welcome, and the Rabbi can set up one-on-one study; see [adult education](/programs/adult-education).

q: Is there a Jewish women's group in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: Yes. The Jewish Women's Circle at Chabad of Lamorinda holds creative evenings, challah bakes and workshops for every woman, whatever her background. To hear about the next one, [join our weekly email](/forms/newsletter) and tick "Women's Circle," or call Rebbetzin Tzipora Labkowski at 925-384-7241.

q: Is there a Jewish men's club in Lamorinda?
a: Yes. The Men's Club at Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette brings men together for Bagels, Lox & Tefillin, Scotch & Steaks in the Sukkah, learning and a l'chaim. See [Men's Club](/programs/mens-club) or call 925-384-7242.

q: Are there Jewish teen programs in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: Yes. Chabad of Lamorinda's teen programs are open to students from Acalanes, Campolindo and Miramonte high schools and the middle schools in all three towns, with past favorites like Krav Maga for Teens and the Rabbi's Kitchen. Teens can also [volunteer](/forms/volunteer); call 925-384-7242 to hear what is coming up.

q: Where can I volunteer in the Jewish community in Lamorinda?
a: At Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette, an hour or a season at a time: help with holiday events, setting up the sukkah, baking challah, Kiddush setup, visiting seniors and the sick, driving, tutoring, photography or office help. [Sign up here](/forms/volunteer).

q: Can I donate to Chabad of Lamorinda by Venmo, Zelle, stock or a donor advised fund?
a: Yes, and every gift is tax deductible. Give [online](/donate), on Venmo to @CHABAD-LAMORINDA, by check to Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette, CA 94549, or through a donor advised fund (tax ID 47-4642750). For Zelle, stock, cryptocurrency or wire transfers, call 925-384-7242 or email info@chabadoflamorinda.com.

q: Do I have to be religious to go to Chabad of Lamorinda?
a: Not at all. Jews of every background and level of observance come to Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette, just as they are. There are no dues and no test, and questions are always welcome.

q: Who can I call for a bris in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: Call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski at 925-384-7242 soon after the birth. The bris is on the eighth day; he helps set the correct date, arranges a qualified mohel and plans the honors and blessings, and a baby girl is named at the Torah. See [new baby](/help/new-baby).

q: Can a Rabbi do a Jewish wedding in Lamorinda?
a: Yes. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski officiates at Jewish weddings according to Jewish law and helps with the date, the ketubah and the chuppah, and the Rebbetzin helps the bride prepare for the mikvah. Call 925-384-7242 as early as you can, ideally several months ahead; see [getting married](/help/getting-married).

q: Can a Rabbi visit someone in the hospital near Martinez?
a: Yes. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski visits at home, in hospitals, care facilities and hospice across our area, including Martinez, Pleasant Hill and Lamorinda. Call 925-384-7242, and we will add your loved one's name to our [Tehillim prayer list](/tehillim); see [someone is sick](/help/someone-is-sick).

q: Can I talk to a Rabbi privately in Lamorinda?
a: Yes. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski meets with anyone, about anything, in confidence and at no charge, and many women prefer to speak with Rebbetzin Tzipora Labkowski. Call 925-384-7242 or see [talk to the Rabbi](/help/talk-to-the-rabbi).

q: What time is candle lighting in Lafayette this Friday?
a: The [Shabbat page](/shabbat) shows this week's candle lighting and Shabbat end times for Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda. Candle lighting is 18 minutes before sunset, and Shabbat ends at nightfall.

q: How can I find Jewish events in Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda?
a: See the [events calendar](/events) for Shabbat dinners, holiday celebrations and classes at Chabad of Lamorinda, add them to your phone with the [calendar subscription](/events.ics), or [get our weekly email](/forms/newsletter) with Shabbat times and what is coming up.

q: How can I sponsor a Kiddush in Lafayette for a yahrzeit or birthday?
a: [Sponsor the Shabbat Kiddush](/sponsor-a-kiddush) at Chabad of Lamorinda and the whole community celebrates with you after Saturday services; your dedication is announced and shown on the Kiddush board. See more ways to mark an occasion on the [sponsor page](/sponsor).

q: What time does Shabbat start in Orinda this week?
a: Shabbat begins at candle lighting on Friday, 18 minutes before sunset, and ends at nightfall on Saturday; this week's times and the next 12 months for Orinda are on [Shabbat times in Orinda](/shabbat-times/orinda). Join us a few minutes away at Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette, for Kabbalat Shabbat on Friday at {kabbalat-shabbat} (the time may change with the season) and services Saturday at 10:00 AM.

q: What time does Shabbat end in Moraga on Saturday night?
a: Shabbat ends at nightfall, and the exact time for Moraga every week, with Havdalah and candle lighting for the next 12 months, is on [Shabbat times in Moraga](/shabbat-times/moraga). Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette, about ten minutes up Moraga Road, holds Shabbat services Saturday 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM with a hot Kiddush lunch.

q: When is candle lighting in Pleasant Hill or Martinez?
a: See [Shabbat times in Pleasant Hill](/shabbat-times/pleasant-hill) and [Shabbat times in Martinez](/shabbat-times/martinez) for candle lighting (18 minutes before sunset) and the time Shabbat ends, for the next 12 months. For services and Shabbat dinner, Chabad of Lamorinda at 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette, is about 15 minutes from Pleasant Hill and 20 minutes from Martinez.

q: Is there a Jewish preschool near Moraga or Orinda?
a: Yes. [Lamorinda Jewish Preschool](/programs/jewish-preschool) at Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette, about ten minutes from Moraga and a few minutes from Orinda, has a class for 12 to 24 months and a class for 2 to 4 years. It runs Monday to Thursday 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM and Friday 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM; [schedule a tour](/forms/preschool) or call 925-384-7242.

q: Who can do a Jewish baby naming in Contra Costa County?
a: Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski of Chabad of Lamorinda names baby girls at the Torah in Lafayette, usually at the first Torah reading after the birth, on a Monday, Thursday or Shabbat, and helps families choose a Hebrew name. Call 925-384-7242 to arrange it, and see [new baby](/help/new-baby).

q: Where can I get kosher meat delivered in the East Bay?
a: Order kosher meat and poultry, groceries and holiday foods online from [Bay Kosher](/programs/bay-kosher), a project of Chabad of Lamorinda, and have it delivered. For help setting up a kosher kitchen, see [kosher in Lamorinda](/learn/kosher-in-lamorinda) or call the Rabbi at 925-384-7242.

q: Is there a Torah class in Hebrew near Walnut Creek or Concord?
a: Yes. Every Tuesday from 8:30 to 9:30 PM, Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski teaches a Torah class in Hebrew, with a meal, at Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette. Every level is welcome; see [adult education](/programs/adult-education).

q: Where can my teen volunteer Jewishly in Lamorinda?
a: At Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette, teens from Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda help with holiday events, setting up the sukkah, baking challah, Kiddush setup, tutoring younger kids and photography. [Sign up here](/forms/volunteer), and see [Jewish teens in Lamorinda](/learn/jewish-teens-in-lamorinda).

q: How do I find my Hebrew birthday?
a: Enter your date of birth in our free [Hebrew birthday calculator](/tools/hebrew-birthday), and save it in [your account](/account) for a reminder every year. Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette can arrange an aliyah on the Shabbat before your Hebrew birthday; call 925-384-7242.

q: When is Chanukah 2026?
a: Chanukah 2026 begins with the first candle on the evening of Friday, December 4, and ends on Saturday, December 12. Every holiday date is on [Jewish holidays 2026](/jewish-holidays-2026), and Chabad of Lamorinda's celebrations are on the [Chanukah page](/holidays/chanukah).

q: When is Chanukah 2027?
a: Chanukah 2027 begins with the first candle on the evening of Friday, December 24, 2027, and ends on Saturday, January 1, 2028. See [Jewish holidays 2027](/jewish-holidays-2027) for every date and candle lighting time in Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda.

q: When is Passover 2027?
a: Passover 2027 begins at sundown on Wednesday, April 21, 2027, the night of the first Seder, and ends on Thursday, April 29. See [Jewish holidays 2027](/jewish-holidays-2027), and the [Passover page](/holidays/passover) for Chabad of Lamorinda's community Seder, Seder-to-go kits and shmurah matzah.

q: When are Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur in 2027?
a: Rosh Hashanah 2027 begins at sundown on Friday, October 1, and is on October 2 and 3; Yom Kippur begins at sundown on Sunday, October 10, and is on Monday, October 11. See [Jewish holidays 2027](/jewish-holidays-2027), and [reserve a seat](/forms/high-holidays) at Chabad of Lamorinda's services in Lafayette, with no tickets or membership needed.

q: When is Purim 2027?
a: Purim 2027 is on Tuesday, March 23, beginning at sundown on Monday, March 22. Chabad of Lamorinda holds Megillah readings, a Purim party and a kids' hamantashen bake in Lafayette; see [Purim](/holidays/purim) and [Jewish holidays 2027](/jewish-holidays-2027).

q: When is Shavuot 2027?
a: Shavuot 2027 begins at sundown on Thursday, June 10, and is on June 11 and 12. At Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette the whole family hears the Ten Commandments, followed by an ice cream and cheesecake party; see [Shavuot](/holidays/shavuot) and [Jewish holidays 2027](/jewish-holidays-2027).

q: Where can I see all the Jewish holiday dates for this year?
a: [Jewish holidays 2026](/jewish-holidays-2026) and [Jewish holidays 2027](/jewish-holidays-2027) list every holiday with its date, Hebrew date and candle lighting time for Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda. Jewish holidays begin at sundown the evening before, and Chabad of Lamorinda's celebrations are on the [events calendar](/events).

q: Can someone say Kaddish for my parent if I cannot?
a: Yes. Chabad of Lamorinda can arrange for Kaddish to be said on your behalf at the minyan in Lafayette; request it at [Kaddish](/kaddish) or call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski at 925-384-7242. You are also welcome to say it yourself at the morning minyan, Monday to Friday at 6:30 AM and Sunday at 8:00 AM.

q: Who can help arrange a shiva minyan in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: Call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski at 925-384-7242. Chabad of Lamorinda helps families set up the shiva home, arranges a minyan for prayers and guides you through the customs; see [when a loved one passes away](/help/someone-passed-away) and our [shiva guide](/learn/shiva).

q: How do I share a Mazal Tov or a shiva notice with the Jewish community in Lamorinda?
a: Send it through the [community page](/community) of Chabad of Lamorinda; Mazal Tovs, announcements and shiva notices are shared once the Rabbi approves them. For help with a shiva itself, call 925-384-7242.

q: Can I plan a Jewish funeral in advance near Lafayette?
a: Yes. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski of Chabad of Lamorinda is glad to sit with you privately, with no pressure, to explain what is involved and help you plan, so your wishes and Jewish tradition are honored. Call 925-384-7242 and see [planning a Jewish funeral](/help/planning-a-jewish-funeral).

q: Does Judaism allow cremation?
a: Jewish law calls for burial, and cremation, like embalming, is against Jewish law; the body is returned to the earth whole and with dignity. Before signing anything with a funeral home, call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski at 925-384-7242, and see [cremation: the Jewish view](/learn/cremation-jewish-view).

q: Where can I immerse new dishes (tevilat kelim) near Lafayette?
a: Call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski at 925-384-7242: he will tell you which of your new dishes need immersion and where to immerse them. Read the basics first in our [tevilat kelim guide](/learn/tevilat-kelim).

q: Is there a mikvah near Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: For private, caring guidance on mikvah, including where to go and how to prepare, call Rebbetzin Tzipora Labkowski of Chabad of Lamorinda at 925-384-7241; every conversation is confidential. See our [mikvah guide](/learn/mikvah).

q: At what age is a bar mitzvah or bat mitzvah?
a: A boy becomes bar mitzvah at 13 and a girl becomes bat mitzvah at 12, on their Hebrew birthday, which can differ from the English date. Find it with the [Bar/Bat Mitzvah calculator](/tools/bar-bat-mitzvah), and call Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette at 925-384-7242 about a year ahead to start lessons.

q: How do I convert to Judaism in the East Bay?
a: Conversion according to Jewish law is a sincere, lifelong commitment, completed before a recognized Beth Din after a long period of study, and every case is personal, so ask the Rabbi. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski of Chabad of Lamorinda is happy to have an honest, confidential conversation; call 925-384-7242 and see [converting to Judaism](/learn/converting-to-judaism).

q: How can I give tzedakah in memory of a loved one in Lafayette?
a: On the [sponsor page](/sponsor) you can dedicate the Shabbat Kiddush, a Shabbat dinner, a Torah class or a children's program at Chabad of Lamorinda in memory of your loved one, and the Rabbi mentions your dedication. Every gift is tax deductible.

q: Is Chabad of Lamorinda building a permanent home?
a: Yes. The Building Campaign will create a permanent home for Jewish life in Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda, and every level of giving is recognized, starting at $1,800. Give through the [donate page](/donate) or call 925-384-7242.

q: Can I host a Shabbat meal for newcomers or students in Lamorinda?
a: Yes. Fill in the [Shabbat meal form](/forms/shabbat-meal) and choose "Host guests for a Shabbat meal," and Chabad of Lamorinda will match you with new families, students from Saint Mary's College and Diablo Valley College, or people on their own.

q: I just moved to Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda. How do I find the Jewish community?
a: Start at our [welcome page](/welcome): come for Shabbat at Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette (Saturday 10 AM, with a hot Kiddush lunch), create a free account, and find a place for your kids. Call Rabbi Yisroel or Rebbetzin Tzipora Labkowski at 925-384-7242; we would love to welcome you personally.

q: Is there an Israeli community in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: Israelis and Hebrew speakers meet at Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette at the Tuesday Torah class in Hebrew (8:30 PM, with a meal), at Shabbat and at the holidays, and kids learn modern Hebrew at CKids Afterschool. See [Israelis in Lamorinda](/learn/israelis-in-lamorinda) or call 925-384-7242.

q: Is the Chabad of Lamorinda website in Hebrew or Russian?
a: Yes. The whole site is in English, Hebrew and Russian: your phone's language is chosen automatically, and you can switch at the top of any page. Shabbat times, events, holidays, help pages and forms all appear in your language; see [Russian-speaking Jews in Lamorinda](/learn/russian-speaking-jews-in-lamorinda).

q: Is there a morning minyan near Orinda BART?
a: Yes. Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way, close to the Lafayette BART station, one stop from Orinda, holds Shacharit Monday to Friday at 6:30 AM and Sunday at 8:00 AM. It is a good time to put on tefillin with the Rabbi; see [Jewish men in Lamorinda](/learn/jewish-men-in-lamorinda).

q: Is there a Lag BaOmer event in Lafayette?
a: Yes. Chabad of Lamorinda holds a Lag BaOmer BBQ in Lafayette. In 2027 Lag BaOmer is on Tuesday, May 25; see [Lag BaOmer](/holidays/lag-baomer) and the [events calendar](/events) for the time and place.

q: How can I sponsor a night of Chanukah in Lamorinda?
a: Be a Chanukah lamplighter: sponsor a night of Chabad of Lamorinda's community menorah, lit at the grand menorah lighting and community celebration. See the [Chanukah page](/holidays/chanukah) or call 925-384-7242.

q: What is the Torah portion this week?
a: See [this week's parsha](/parsha) and [this week in Jewish Lamorinda](/this-week), with Shabbat times for every town and the Jewish dates. The weekly Torah portion is taught on Sunday from 9:00 to 10:00 PM at Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette.

q: What are today's prayer times (zmanim) in Lafayette?
a: Our [zmanim tool](/tools/zmanim) shows the daily Jewish prayer times for Lafayette, and the [Hebrew date converter](/tools/hebrew-date) gives any day's Jewish date. Chabad of Lamorinda's morning minyan is Monday to Friday at 6:30 AM and Sunday at 8:00 AM.

q: Where can I add a name to a prayer list for someone who is sick?
a: Add your loved one's name to Chabad of Lamorinda's [Tehillim prayer list](/tehillim), and the Rabbi says a Mi Shebeirach for them at the Torah reading in Lafayette. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski also visits at home and in hospitals; call 925-384-7242 and see [someone is sick](/help/someone-is-sick).

q: Can I ask a Rabbi a question about Judaism online?
a: Yes. [Ask the Rabbi](/ask) any question about Jewish life online, or call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski of Chabad of Lamorinda at 925-384-7242 to talk in person, in confidence and at no charge. See [talk to the Rabbi](/help/talk-to-the-rabbi).

q: Is there a daytime Jewish class for seniors near Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: Yes. The Tanya class meets Wednesday from 1:00 to 2:00 PM at Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette, and every level is welcome. See [Jewish seniors in Lamorinda](/learn/jewish-seniors-in-lamorinda).

q: Can I bring my kids to Shabbat services in Lafayette?
a: Please do. Children take part in Shabbat morning services at Chabad of Lamorinda every Saturday from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM and stay for the hot Kiddush lunch; see [Shabbat with kids](/learn/shabbat-with-kids).

q: Who can I talk to about grief or loneliness in the Jewish community near Lafayette?
a: Call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski or Rebbetzin Tzipora Labkowski of Chabad of Lamorinda at 925-384-7242; they meet with anyone, in confidence, and would love to have you at their Shabbat table. See [grief, loneliness and hard times](/help/grief-and-hard-times).

q: I am visiting family in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda for Shabbat. Where can I go?
a: Visitors are always welcome at Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette: Kabbalat Shabbat Friday evening and services Saturday at 10:00 AM with a hot Kiddush lunch. [RSVP for Shabbat dinner](/forms/shabbat-meal) with the Rabbi's family and see [visiting Lamorinda](/learn/visiting-lamorinda).

q: How can I get reminders for yahrzeits and Hebrew birthdays?
a: Save your family's Hebrew names, birthdays and yahrzeits in a free [Chabad of Lamorinda account](/account). The site then sends yahrzeit, Hebrew birthday and bar or bat mitzvah reminders, and gives you a private calendar link of your family's Jewish dates.

q: Who can help with an upsherin in Lamorinda?
a: Call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski of Chabad of Lamorinda at 925-384-7242 and he will help make your son's first haircut at age three a joyful, meaningful celebration. See our [upsherin guide](/learn/upsherin).

q: What time is Kabbalat Shabbat in Lafayette on Friday night?
a: This week Kabbalat Shabbat at Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette, begins at {kabbalat-shabbat}. The time follows the season so that it never starts after sunset: close to candle lighting in the winter, and 6:45 PM through the summer. Everyone from Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda is welcome, with no membership; see [Shabbat times and services](/shabbat).

q: How do I light the Chanukah menorah on Friday before Shabbat?
a: Light the menorah first, a little before the Shabbat candles, using candles or oil that will burn until at least half an hour after nightfall; then light the Shabbat candles at candle lighting time. On Saturday night, make Havdalah first and then light the menorah. Step by step: [Chanukah on Shabbat](/learn/chanukah-on-shabbat). Questions? Call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski at 925-384-7242.

q: What is Yud Tes Kislev?
a: The 19th of Kislev, the "Rosh Hashanah of Chassidus," celebrates the release from prison of the Alter Rebbe, the founder of Chabad, in 1798. It is marked with farbrengens, Chassidic gatherings with stories, songs and Torah. Read more in our [Yud Tes Kislev guide](/learn/yud-tes-kislev), and call Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette at 925-384-7242 to join a farbrengen or a Tanya class.

q: Can a rabbi help settle a family or business dispute in Lafayette?
a: Yes. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski of Chabad of Lamorinda, 3477 Golden Gate Way in Lafayette, helps with every kind of dispute: between spouses, parents and children, siblings, in-laws, neighbors, business partners, clients and employees, and with great success. Come early, before things spiral; and it is never too late. He listens privately, guides by the Torah, mediates when both sides agree, and refers to a Beth Din when needed. Call or WhatsApp 925-384-7242, or see [disputes](/help/disputes).

q: Where is the mikvah near Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda?
a: Women in Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda generally use the Chabad mikvah in Berkeley. To arrange a visit, or for kallah classes and any private question, call or text Rebbetzin Tzipora Labkowski of Chabad of Lamorinda at 925-384-7241. See [mikvah](/learn/mikvah).

q: How do I find my Bar Mitzvah parshah?
a: Enter the birth date on our [Bar and Bat Mitzvah parshah finder](/tools/bar-bat-mitzvah) and it shows the Hebrew date and the Torah portion, for a coming Bar or Bat Mitzvah or for your own from years ago. For lessons and planning in Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda, call Rabbi Labkowski at 925-384-7242.

q: Why do we light candles on Friday before Shabbat?
a: Lighting candles brings light and peace into the home as Shabbat begins; it is a special mitzvah for Jewish women and girls, done 18 minutes before sunset on Friday with a blessing. This week's time for Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda is on our [Shabbat times](/shabbat-times) page, and the step by step is in [Shabbat candles](/learn/shabbat-candles). Need candles? Ask Chabad of Lamorinda.

q: What is cholent?
a: Cholent is the slow-cooked stew of meat, beans and potatoes that simmers from Friday afternoon until Shabbat lunch, so there is a hot meal without cooking on Shabbat. At Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette there is hot cholent at the Kiddush after Shabbat services every Saturday, and everyone is welcome. See [Shabbat at Chabad](/shabbat).

q: What is Kiddush?
a: Kiddush is the blessing over wine that sanctifies Shabbat and holidays, said Friday night and again Saturday after services. At Chabad of Lamorinda it is also the warm lunch after Shabbat services, open to everyone. How to make it at home: [Kiddush](/learn/kiddush).

q: What is Havdalah?
a: Havdalah is the short ceremony on Saturday night that ends Shabbat, with wine, sweet-smelling spices and a braided candle. It is said after nightfall; this week's time is on our [Shabbat times](/shabbat-times) page, and the words and steps are in [Havdalah](/learn/havdalah).

q: What does Shabbat Shalom mean?
a: Shabbat Shalom means “a peaceful Shabbat”, the greeting from Friday afternoon until Saturday night. On Saturday night people say Shavua Tov, “a good week”. Come say it in person at [Shabbat at Chabad](/shabbat) in Lafayette.

q: Can a rabbi visit a dying relative in hospice in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: Yes. Call Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski at 925-384-7242 (or the Rebbetzin at 925-384-7241). We will help you be with your loved one, say the Shema and Vidui, and guide you through every step. See [when a loved one is dying](/learn/when-a-loved-one-is-dying).

q: What should a Jewish person do before surgery?
a: Ask the Rabbi for a blessing and have a Mi Sheberach said with your Hebrew name, say Tehillim (chapters 20 and 121), give tzedakah and check your mezuzahs. Call Rabbi Labkowski at 925-384-7242. See [before surgery](/learn/prayer-before-surgery).

q: When do Jews start praying for rain in the US?
a: Outside Israel, the request for rain (“v’ten tal u’matar”) is added to the weekday Amidah from the evening of December 4 (December 5 in the year before a leap year) until Passover. See [prayers for rain](/learn/prayers-for-rain), or ask Rabbi Labkowski at Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette, 925-384-7242.

q: Is there a Chanukah menorah lighting guide online?
a: Yes: [Light the menorah](/menorah) shows which candles to light each night, in what order, the blessings in Hebrew, transliteration and English, and tonight’s lighting time for Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda.

q: Can a rabbi visit my parent with dementia in a memory care home in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: Yes. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski (925-384-7242) or the Rebbetzin (925-384-7241) can visit your parent at home or in memory care, bring Shabbat or a holiday to them, and pray with them. See [when a parent has dementia](/learn/when-a-parent-has-dementia).

q: How can I get through Chanukah or the holidays after losing someone, in Lafayette, Moraga or Orinda?
a: You do not have to do it alone. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski (925-384-7242) and the Rebbetzin (925-384-7241) are glad to talk, by phone or in person, and you are welcome at Shabbat and holiday events at Chabad of Lamorinda. See [grief during the holidays](/learn/grief-during-the-holidays) for ideas that help.

q: What is Hey Teves (5 Tevet) and how do Chabad families celebrate it?
a: Hey Teves marks the 1987 court ruling that the Chabad Rebbes' library belongs to the Chassidic community. It is celebrated by buying a new Jewish book and learning from it that day. For a suggestion, ask Rabbi Labkowski at 925-384-7242. See [Hey Teves](/learn/hey-teves).

q: What is the purpose of life according to Judaism?
a: Judaism teaches that every person is here on purpose: to make this world a home for G-d through good deeds, mitzvot and kindness, each in their own place. Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski at Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette (925-384-7242) is glad to talk about life's big questions. See [why am I here?](/learn/purpose-of-life).

q: Can I pray to G-d in English, in my own words?
a: Yes. G-d understands every language, and a sincere prayer in your own words, anytime and anywhere, is a real prayer. See [talking to G-d in your own words](/learn/talking-to-g-d-in-your-own-words), or call Rabbi Labkowski at 925-384-7242.

q: What is the Friday night blessing for children, and how do I say it?
a: Before Kiddush on Friday night, parents place their hands on each child's head and say "Yesimcha Elo-him k'Efrayim v'chi-Menasheh" for a son or "Yesimech Elo-him k'Sarah, Rivkah, Rachel v'Leah" for a daughter, followed by the Priestly Blessing. See [blessing your children](/learn/blessing-your-children), or see it done at a Shabbat dinner at Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette (925-384-7242).

q: What blessing do I say after surgery or a dangerous trip?
a: Birkat HaGomel, the blessing of thanks, said in synagogue in front of a minyan, usually at the Torah reading. Come to Shabbat services at Chabad of Lamorinda in Lafayette, or call Rabbi Labkowski at 925-384-7242 to arrange it. See [Birkat HaGomel](/learn/birkat-hagomel).
